notes:
Customer snapshot: small/medium gov contracting org that handles archived FOIA/regulatory packages + classified attachments in segregated air-gapped enclaves. Primary need: searchable RAG layer across mixed corpora (documents, scanned PDFs, forensic images). Emphasis on embeddings + reranking to keep top-K precision high under strict latency SLOs.

Main asks / constraints:
- On-prem deployment inside an air-gapped enclave; cannot call hosted endpoints.
- Must support FIPS-compatible KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys.
- Data residency: documents cannot leave facility; strict retention & audit controls.
- Index scale: ~120M text+ocr segments initially, upper bound 500M in 18 months.
- Query profile: 600 qps sustained peak across operations window, burst to 2k qps for incident response events.
- Latency SLO: median <120ms, P95 <350ms for initial top-K retrieval + rerank.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement expects predictable TCO for a 3-year CAPEX + annual maintenance model.
- Models: prefer quantized open models for embedding generation (512/768 dims) and a small reranker (LLM or cross-encoder) on GPU for top-50 candidates.

Engagement history / timeline (high level):
- 2025-11-04: Lead created after intro from channel partner (secure-solver).
- 2025-11-11: Intro call (AE Marcus Chen) — reviewed architecture, customer constraint list.
- 2025-12-02: Security questionnaire sent (legal + infosec).
- 2026-01-15: Technical deep-dive (SE Leah Gomez) — discussed embedding vector size, sharding, approximate nearest neighbor: HNSW vs IVF+PQ tradeoffs. Fireflies: ff_2026-01-15_cp_intro.
- 2026-01-30: Initial POC scoping: sample dataset (2M segments) for perf baseline; test on-prem deployment via air-gapped install kit.
- 2026-02-05: Pricing draft v1 uploaded (/drive/pricing/copperpine_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf).
- 2026-02-12: Security deep dive with their compliance team; requested HSM/KMS proof-of-concept (HSM rotation & key destruction workflows). Fireflies: ff_2026-02-12_security_deepdive.
- 2026-02-20: Procurement engaged; security packet in legal review. Support ticket opened for on-prem installer quirks (INFRA-1134).

Technical notes from SE sessions (shorthand):
- Embeddings: customer's preferred pipeline uses 768-d vectors; evaluating 512 to reduce index size. Need clear guidance from Redwood Optimize on quantization tradeoffs and embedding distillation possibility.
- Indexing: want incremental index updates with immutable segment ids; snapshot-based replication to air-gapped DR site. Concern about index rebuild time at 200M+.
- ANN: HNSW mem footprint is a worry; suggestion: hybrid approach — IVF+PQ for global recall, HNSW for hot partitions. Discussed 8-bit PQ and custom shard placement logic.
- Reranking: plan to run cross-encoder reranker on a small GPU pool. Target rerank depth 50-100 to balance latency/cost. Need fallback to CPU light reranker for degraded mode.
- Caching: heavy prefix/KV caching recommended for investigatory flows (repeated queries).
- Monitoring: need token-level cost visibility removed (customer wants masked metrics) and long retention on audit logs (7+ years).

Quotes / customer language: "If we can't guarantee data never leaves the enclave, procurement will nix it." — Head of Ops.

Open action items / next steps (short):
- Prepare air-gapped deployment checklist and customer-specific installer build (due 2026-03-03).
- Deliver refined TCO workbook with CAPEX/OPEX split and quantization savings scenarios (Marcus).
- Legal: finalize KMS/HSM attestation and contract language; loop in Redwood security for ISO/SOC docs.
- Schedule on-site security demo and ops runbook review week of 2026-03-10 (tentative).

POC plan (scoped): 6-week on-prem POC using 2M segments -> benchmark indexing throughput, embedding generation throughput, ANN recall @top-100, rerank latency & cost-per-query. Acceptance criteria: top-10 precision >= 0.82 on eval set; median end-to-end latency <150ms; deterministic install in air-gapped environment.

Risks called out: procurement timeline (6–12 months), potential requirement to use customer-approved hardware images only (delays installer validation), competitor (Palantir) already in vendor evaluation list.

CRM style notes: preference for short updates in thread; echoing questions from compliance team in case notes; use numbered attachments for legal artifacts.
